analysis:
Only docs/architecture/inference.md is changed. The date bump is at line 3 on the head side. The substantive edit is in the GLM5Next video paragraph (head lines ~810-829). It documents that variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime video is now indexed at i / nominalFrameRate instead of being refused with a 400. The matching sentence about processor refusals no longer lists variable-frame-rate video. A further hunk at head lines 876-880 is only partly visible: the patch excerpt is truncated and the supplied head text covers lines 1-415 only. The supplied base excerpt covers the Flint section and nothing around the changed GLM lines. I could not inspect the lines that changed (810-829, 876-880) on either side, nor the head GLM section.

This is documentation only. No source, protocol, or threat-model definition changed in the supplied evidence, so I found no code-level regression. The documented behavior change could carry security implications if the source change was shipped in the same PR. Examples are a larger decode or memory surface from VFR clips, or timing semantics that diverge from the processor. The documented bounds still apply: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (`maximumDecodedBytes`), the 28,532 visual-token cap, and the media reservation (`GLM5NextVisionBudget.mediaReservation`). These remain unverified here because the Swift code (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset) is not in the supplied units.

Relevant threat IDs that a source reviewer should consider are T-050 (inline video plaintext in temp files) and TB-007/T-029 (resource exhaustion). The doc claims media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so there is no cross-tenant KV reuse from media; this is consistent with T-041. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the VFR acceptance in the source keeps the cap and reservation checks and does not write decoded video to temp files.
